Kanawana 


DIRECTOR'S ANNUAL REPORT 


KAMP_KANAWANA_1976 


DIRECTOR'S REPORT 


Kamp Kanawana 1976 has come to an end. It was personally my 
best of the last four years at Kamp. | have many fond memories 
of the past summer. There were, of course, the usual ups and 
downs as we progressed through the elght weeks. 


In this report, | will try to give the reader my honest 
Impresston of this summer at Kamp Kanawana as well as Indicate 
some of the areas requiring attentlon for '77. 


KAMPERS 


This summer we worked with 480 different children from six 
different provinces and seven different countries. The YMCA 
sponsored more than thirty underprivileged children this summer. 


Our registration surpassed our budgeted amount of 1250 kamper 
weeks with a total of 1358 (1356 In '75 and 1264 In "74). Our 
returnee rate decreased slightly to an average of 44.8%, 


See Appendix A. 
STAFE 


The Kamp Kanawana '76 staff had to be one of the best, If not 
the best of many years. The average age of program staff 
Increased to 21.6 years with a returnee rate of 63%. If 1s 
noteworthy to mention that 28 out of 5I program staff had thelr 
bronze medallion lifesaving (R.L.S.S.) or better. 


For varlous reasons, four staff members resigned during the 
summer. This Its not new or untlque to Kamp Kanawana. However, 
| accept this as one of the current difficulties with Kamp 
staff recrultment. 


A spectal thank you to my assistant Andy Elifot for his patience, 
support and hard work this summer. This was Andy's first time 

In this capacity for which he deserves a lot of credit. | know 
from past experlence that It was not easy. Mercl Andy! 


Staff continued 2 


The majority of the staff did excellent jobs with our kampers 
+his summer. Thetr patience, determination and mature out look 
on thelr work made this summer's staff team a most effective one. 


My sincere thanks to them for a huge job well done.

STAFF TRAINING 4 


The pre-kamp training program this year was more condensed than 
in previous years. It proved successful as it prepared the 
staff as well as it was possible in seven days. It also quickly 
developed a Kamp splIrit. 
A few suggestion for next summer: 

- again Insist that all staff participate in all sessions. 


- have only one day between the end of pre-kamp and the 
arrival of the kampers (f.e. lengthen It). 


- more first ald, child psychology, lifesaving. 
- have a longer canoe trip. 


- bring back the sessions in St. Hilaire 
(my fault | contacted them too late). 


In addition, we sent the following to training programs: 
- Rob Wiltshire, Woodsmanship School, Toronto 
- Nancy Sawyer, Canoe Tripper's School, Toronto 
- Misty McKay, Vermont Ecology School, Vermont 
This support should be continued as much as possible In the 


future. 


PROGRAM AREAS 


(For more detall, see the Assistant Kamp Director's report and 
that of the staff Involved and also survey or kampers) See App. B. 


Arts & Crafts: 


Stewart Sandmark and his assistant Wendy Prince did an excellent 
job with our Arts & Crafts program this summer. 


Stewart's tlanets together with the acquisition of some new 
equipment encouraged kampers to develop thelr artistic skills. 


Arts & Crafts continued 
The program included: 
making and/or finishing paddles 


carving birds, wooden decorations, games, candle 
holders, etc. 


making furniture 
sketching and painting 
string art 

macrame, etc. 


| cannot help but praise and thank Stewart and his crew for a 
job well done. 


Folk Dancing: 


This program was expertly led by Claude Boucher and Francine 
Gagne. Many kampers, particularly the girls enjoyed learning 
many old French Canadian dances. 


Kampcraft: 


It was good to see kampers baking bread, making fires, setting 
up shelters, etc. In our kampcraft program this summer. 


My thanks to Rob Wiltshire and his kampcraft staff for a great 
program. 


Naturelore: 


Our naturelore program headed by Adele 'Misty' McKay Improved 
greatly over recent years. 


With more emphas!Is on the Kamp's part, It should continue in 
that direction in the future. 


Orienteering: 


Last year's very popular program continued under the direction 
of Rob Darker. A great number of kampers participated and 
recelved Orienteering awards throughout the summer. 


Judo: 


This was a new Interest group this year headed by Jeff Dubney 
(Westmount Y Judo Instructor). It was well received by a small 
number of kampers and could be considered In the future. 


lf it Is to take place, at least 16 mats (rather than 6) will be 
required. 


Drama: 


Headed admirably by Steve Davies and Robin Siegerman, a small 
number of kampers enjoyed the preparation, rehearsal and 
presentation of several small plays in the dining hall. 


Archery: 


Kevin Holgate directed this Interest group. The main requlrement 
for next year Is proper targets. 


Salling: 


Once again, our Sailing Director Dave O'Donnell was Involved 
with the teaching of many kampers the skill of salling. The 
addition of three more Snarks as well as Dave's ability to 
matntatn the boats (and canoes) helped to make the program run 
smoothly. 


Canoeing: 


We were fortunate to have Rob Dewar return to Kamp Kanawana as 
our Canoeing Director. His expertise (and qualifications) In 
canoeing Improved the program tremendously. 


Rob and his Instructors should be congratulated for the quality 
and quantity of Instruction that took place at the canoe sltp 
this summer. 


Boating: 


Due to the other aquatic alternatives present at Kamp our 
Boating Instructors Philip Ching and Helen Caravolas did a good 
job with a small number of participants In this instruction. 


Waterfronts: 


The senior and junior waterfronts were directed by Kathy 
Livingstone and Steve Bauman respectively. 


Unfortunately, the weather was never very cooperative and this 
made the varlous water Instructions difficult to complete. 
Nevertheless, both did a fine job and many kampers went home 
thrilled with the accomplishment of learning how to swim. 
Thanks to them both for a job well done. 


It ts worth noting that under Coach Elliot, our Kamp Kanawana 
'Swim Team! won the 1976 Camp Pembina swim meet (with 4 other 
camps). Congratulations to all Involved! 


The only disappointment would be the fact that not one of our 
C.1.T.s completed the Bronze Lifesaving course. 


Hike & Trip: 


What a summer It was! After over 14,000 miles on the Kamp van 
In 7 weeks, over 85 trips were sent out. These Included the 
‘local' trips on Kamp property to extensive canoe trips in 

such areas as Papineau-Labelle Park, Manewan Indian Reservation, 
Kempt Lake, 3! Mile Lake, back packing trips to Mont Marcy [fn 
Vermont and war canoe trips from Mont Laurter to Ottawa and then 
Ottawa to Montreal. 


The program was boosted with the addition of several more canoes 
as well as various equipment from Wilderness Survival Camp. 


The direction of the Hike and Trip program came again this year 
from Dick MIischook. Considering the weather and the once agaln 
Increased popularity of tripping he and his staff did an even 
better job this year in coping with the demand. 


| am sure many staff and kampers share my opinion and thank Dick 
and his crew for the fine tripping program this year. 


This summer was the first for the new Kamp Kanawana award "Order 
of Owens". This was presented by Norrey Owens to the kamper who 
best exemplified the qualities and attributes of a tripper at 

Kanawana. My congratulations to the tripper of 1976, Doug Peets. 


General Program: 


For the first part of the summer, a 3 day rather than daily method 

of schedullng was used. In theory, the Idea Is good but In practice, 
never really worked. Hence, the dally method should be used next 
year. 


| and some other staff have doubts about the validity of the 
Lumbermen=-Voyageur program. It is a very different style (i.e. 
ultra competition) of program as compared to the regular Kamp 
Kanawana programs. It also interfers with the best of the tripping 
season. Its continuing should be thoroughly discussed and decided 
this winter. 


Questions have been raised in regards to Kamp Kanawana on co-= 
educational programs. The amount (or lack thereof) of co-ed 
programs has been gauged by myself. | suggest a group of staff 
develop some sort of recommendations for our operation next summer. 


At times, the staff had difficulties with some of our elght week 
kampers. Either the program for these must be Improved or we 
should limit a stay to four weeks. This should be looked at this 
winter. 


We have had many years of experience with running Kanawana. 
However, we have not yet managed to develop a proper file of 
program resources and ideas, etc. This should be one of the 
program priorities In preparing for Kamp Kanawana '77, 


COUNSELLOR-|IN-TRAINING PROGRAM 


One of our weaknesses this summer was the C.!/.T. program. 
Unfortunately, our C.1/.1T. Director left Kamp after 4 weeks and 

many of our objectives for the program were not achieved. It Is 

my optnton that the C.1.T.s this year did not gain from the program 
as In years past and consequently, not as many are ready to assume 
staff positions with Kanawana. 


Itche Kerr took over the program and did an admirable job with 
sessions on group dynamics, skill programs, etc. | believe, If we 
are to continue with this or a similar program, some very serious 
questions must be asked before It Is attempted again. 


HEALTH & SAFETY 9 


In sptte of the summer being wet and cold compared to the sun of 
'75, we encountered fewer I!nesses amongst kampers and staff. 


There are, however, a couple of things to mention here - there was 
(as often happens In camps) a 'bug' at Kamp this summer. It had 
been diagnosed as viral meningitis and affected at least 19 people 
including myself. Three people at Kamp (2 being staff) were 
hospItalized for a minimum of 6 days. 


This summer was the first time In many years that Kanawana had a 
Doctor (Seymour Blum) In resiagence. This very much eased the 
driving situation and the presence of a Doctor on the premises 
was reassuring. We should certainly attempt to have a Doctor at 
Kamp again nest year. 


Our Nurse, Sheena Maclean, did an admirable job in coping with the 
general running of the hospital as well as getting Involved fn 
other areas of Kamp. Thank you Sheena. 


Some statistics from this summer: 


Sprains 115 
Sore throats & colds 255 
Ear aches 45 
Cuts & scrapes 281 
X-ray trips 26 
Snake bites 48 
Gastritis 72 
Fractures 7 


FOOD SERVICES 


Our kitchen had its share of difficulttes this summer, For the 
first time in many years, we did not have to replace any of the 
staff in the kitchen with the exception of the Chef. 


By the third session, we were on our fifth Chef with everyone from 
Ed Neal, our Nurse, our assistant chef and myself filling in. It 
was difficult for the kitchen staff but | think thelr more than 
usual involvement In Kamp program throughout the summer enhanced 
their enjoyment of Kamp Kanawana. 


Food Services continued 10 
Due to the changes In the chefs, the menu altered throughout. the 
summer as did the quality and quantity of food. I belleve that 
at least a 30% increase In our food operation budget should be 


considered next year In order to help the staff and food situation 
In the kitchen. 


BUSINESS OFFICE 


The Business Office was wel! managed by Karin Deterding who has 
been on the staff since 1972. Her understanding and Involvement 
wlth Kamp Kanawana made her a real asset to me. | thank her for a 
job well done, 


Two things to note: 


1. We should continue to keep the Business Office 
open all day for staff. 


2. The beverages should be changed to some sort 
of nutritous Julce or perhaps fresh fruit. 
PHYSICAL SITE 
Once again, Julien Tasse and his crew did a super job with 
maintaining dear old Kanawana,. 
Some of the things done include: 


- completing construction of the 'T' on the 
juntor waterfront. 


- completing 2 wash areas. 


- repalring and replacing balconies on the chief's 
cabin, lookout and grand portage. 


- construction of an 'F' satling dock. 


- installation of an ‘alraitor' sewage treatment 
plant in the girls section. 


- installation of a new mixer and exhaust fan In 
the kitchen. 


Physical Site continued | 


- installation of exterlor lighting at the hospital, 
sentor waterfront and Hike & Trip. 


- installation of Interftor lighting in Arts & Crafts. 
- repair and repaint 16 rowboats. 
- repainting and reroofing the cabooses. 


In additton to the above, Is the regular maintenance and patching 
up of many other areas of Kamp. 


With the future rebuilding plans of the existing site soon to 
become reality, some of the very major concerns should be taken 
care of In the future (i.e, water treatment plant, washroom 
facilities, longhouse, etc.). 


There are, however, some things requiring attention before next 
summer and these should be studied, priorized and started as soon 
as possible. 


PROMOT ION 


Due to our relatively secure returnee rate and perhaps a better 
reputation In camping, we reduced our advertising spending from 
$2,000.00 to $120.00 this year. 


The following was done this year for our promotional program: 


- 2500 brochures were malled or distributed 
through local branches. 


- The 'Green Triangle' had six Issues. 


- A Kanawana 'Kalender' was produced and 
distributed to all last year's kampers 
and friends of Kamp. It was extremely 
well received (served as a Xmas card toot) 
and should be continued if time and money 
permit. 


- On behalf of the Quebec Camping Association, 
the Kamp Director was interviewed on CFCF, 
CJAD and CBC radio stations as well as three 
Montreal newspapers. 


- The Kamp Kanawana reunton was held In April 
with over 150 people attending. 


SPECIFIC RECOMMENDATIONS 12 


For the most part, the majority of staff should be rehired. 
There are a few who, for one reason or another, | would be 
apprehensive about rehiring. 


For further detail on the above, the personnel confidential 
flle at the Camp Office should be consulted. 


The 3-day break was tried and didn't work. We should revert 
back to the day off a week for staff and forget about the 
break. 


An attempt was made at post-kamp staff canoe trips this 
summer. I!+t did not succeed due to our late closing. 
It should be considered again next year. 


The rental of a large cargo truck (for luggage) on the third 
change-over proved to make the operation very smooth. lf a 
part-time driver for such a vehicle could be found, it should 
be used at all change-overs. 


| belleve the tnerease In counsellor salaries this summer 
assisted us with our recruitment. This trend should continue 
next year. 


Our staff, for the most part, cooperated In reducing kampers 
smoking. Next year, some sort of permission form with 
explanation of pollctes should be included in our Information 
booklet. 


Due to commitments at the Montreal Office, etc., | did not 
get around to see the staff as much as | would have liked. 
This must change next year. 


CONCLUSION 13 


| said at the beginning of this report that this was personally 
my best year at Kamp Kanawana since | began. For me it is not 
just the 2 months but also the 10 months prior that make it. 


To our kampers, | shall always be indebted to you for it is you 
who make all this worthwhile. 


To Julien and Olga - sincerest thanks. | don't believe that we 
would have done as well as we have without the dedicated work 
and continuous support of these two great Kanawanians. 


To our Kamp staff - again many thanks for a huge job well done. 


| sincerely hope that you enjoyed your experiences this summer 
as | know your kampers did. 


Respectfully submitted, 


Derek V. Walsh, 
Director of Camping. 


APPRECIATION 


The outstanding success year after year at Kanawana depends on 
many, many people beyond the staff of Kamp. Appreciation Is 
expressed to the following for their contribution to Kanawana: 


lvanhoe Corporation for permitting us to use the parking 
lot of the Dorval Gardens Shopping Centre as the Montreal 
terminal for kamper transportation. 


The staff of the Montreal YMCA for their continued 
encouragement and cooperation. 


Our 15 C.1.T.s for their work and assistance at Kamp this 
summer. 


Our many neighbours around Kamp who so willingly permit 
us to use thelr properties and assist us in many ways. 


The Camping Branch Board of Management for their hundreds 
of hours of work in preparing Kamp Kanawana '76. 


The group of Dental HygenIsts who lectured our kampers 
on dental hygene. 


The Drug Companies who so generously donated medications 
and supplies for our Infirmary, Frosst, Horner, Astra, 
Parke-Davis, Squibb and Burroughs-Wel|lcome. 


The Montreal Copy Centre for the various free printings. 


Andy Barrte and CJAD radio for the 15 minute story on 
Kanawana and our giant reunion. 


Westmount, West Island and Downtown Branches for lending 
us their rooms for our meetings. 


1'm trying to find a place, where 
My mind can just let go 
Of all the thoughts of hate, that 


1 am starting to show. 


I've discovered a place, where 
You can hear the breeze 
It drifts quietly across the lake, and 


Rustles through the trees. 


I'm going to a place, where 
| feel very free 
To love, and live, and be myself 


With people a lot like me. 


| think you know the name, of 
This place, that | love 
But, just In case you're not quite sure 


It's Kanawana I'm thinking of. 


Kitti Luce 


Kitt! Luce wrote this poem this summer when she was 
a senior girl kamper.
